newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PdVSA aims for half of Venezuelan gasoline sales.
newsitem.headline: PdVSA aims for half of Venezuelan gasoline sales.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned oil company, Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA), expects to keep only half Venezuela's roadside gasoline sales when it relinquishes its 20 year domestic monopoly under a bill currently waiting congressional discussion, a senior PdVSA official said.
"The opening we're giving to the internal market will reduce our presence to around 40 or 50 percent," Ronald Pantin, vice president of PdVSA affiliate Corpoven, told reporters.
"The rest will be taken-up by national or foreign companies, free to enter the national market and buy direct from refineries," he said.

Venezuela's domestic fuels market accounts for 360,000 barrels per day, of which some 197,000 are gasolines. Under the opening, PdVSA sales will solely handled by the newly created affiliate Deltaven while affiliates Lagoven, Corpoven and Maraven devote themselves only to exploration, production and refining.
